n : Nat as the index of the two real-valued functions compared asymptotically at Filter.atTop
hypotheses: For the equality involving LocalDef002 n at zero, n is strictly positive.
conclusions: For every natural n, the fair binomial PMF with 2n trials assigns its central outcome n the ENNReal mass (1/2)^(2n) times choose(2n,n).

For every positive natural n, the pushforward distribution of a fair binomial count K with 2n trials under K ↦ (K-n)/sqrt(n/2) assigns zero exactly the same mass that the original binomial PMF assigns the central count n.
As n tends to infinity, the real sequence (1/2)^(2n) choose(2n,n) is Theta of the real sequence 1/sqrt(2n).
mathematical_definitions: Let B_n be the binomial probability mass function with 2n trials and success parameter 1/2, supported on the counts 0 through 2n.
The central binomial mass is B_n(n)=(1/2)^(2n) choose(2n,n).
LocalDef002 n is the pushforward of B_n under the real-valued map k ↦ (k-n)/sqrt(n/2).
Asymptotics.IsTheta atTop means that each of the two real-valued sequences is big-O of the other in norm for sufficiently large natural indices.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The center of a fair binomial distribution with an even number 2n of trials has exact probability choose(2n,n)/2^(2n); for n>0 this is also the probability that its centered and normalized transform equals zero; and these central probabilities have asymptotic order 1/sqrt(2n).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The exact binomial mass identity holds for every natural n, including n=0.
The standardized-PMF identity is asserted only for n>0, which excludes the zero normalization denominator sqrt(n/2).

LocalDef002 is a pushforward PMF on Real; its mass at zero includes all original outcomes mapped to zero, and the positive-n restriction makes the displayed central outcome the relevant zero preimage.
The first exact identity is an equality in ENNReal, while the theta comparison uses a separately written real-valued algebraic expression.
The theta conclusion gives only two-sided asymptotic order, not an exact asymptotic constant, a limit, or an error bound.
The comparison function is literally 1/sqrt(2n), not merely 1/sqrt(n), although these differ only by a constant factor.

The denominator 1/sqrt(2n) is undefined in ordinary field notation at n=0 only in the informal sense; in Real it evaluates using totalized division, and the atTop relation ignores finite initial behavior.

The proposition concerns only the central count of the fair binomial distribution and the zero atom of its stated normalization; it does not characterize other counts or the full normalized distribution.
There is no inconsistent antecedent: the only hypothesis is n>0 in the second conjunct, and positive natural numbers exist.
ambiguities: The packet expands IsTheta as mutual norm-based big-O but does not expand the precise witness formulation of Asymptotics.IsBigO.
No probabilistic construction by independent trials is exposed; PMF.binomial is supplied directly as a probability mass function.
The proposition does not state whether an exact limiting constant for sqrt(n) times the central mass is intended beyond the asserted Theta relation.
